back: A sudden rise of water in a dry channel after intense rain, carrying a heavy load and ending quickly.
A gently sloping bedrock surface at the foot of a desert mountain front, formed by sheet floods, stream action and weathering.
Deflation hollows, ventifacts, rock pedestals, yardangs and zeugen.
Barchan (crescent, horns downwind, one wind direction), seif (linear ridge, two wind directions) and star (arms in several directions, grows upwards).
A steep-sided, flat-floored dry river channel cut by flash floods; also called an arroyo.
Flat-topped hills with a resistant cap rock left by scarp retreat; a mesa is broad, and a butte is smaller and narrower.
A fan of gravel and sand deposited where a stream leaves a mountain front; overlapping fans form a bajada.
A flat bed of silt and salt in an inland basin, left by evaporation of temporary lakes; examples are Etosha Pan and the Makgadikgadi Pans.
Q (m³/s) = width (m) × mean depth (m) × mean velocity (m/s).
